newsitem.title: USA: Comforce to acquire Uniforce for $32/shr.
newsitem.headline: Comforce to acquire Uniforce for $32/shr.

text.p: Comforce Corp said Thursday it had agreed to acquire Uniforce Services Inc for about $135 million.
Comforce said it would offer $28 cash plus $4 of Comforce common stock for each outstanding Uniforce share, and would assume $35 million of outstanding Uniforce debt.
Comforce said the agreement provides for a tender offer for Uniforce common, with a follow-up merger resulting in Uniforce becoming a Comforce subsidiary.

The combined companies will be a nationwide provider of specialty staffing, consulting and outsourcing services, focusing on technology-intensive markets, with estimated 1997 revenues of $400 million.

Comforce said it had signed an agreement with the largest single shareholder of Uniforce, who holds about 60 percent of the outstanding shares. Under the pact, the shareholder will tender his shares in the Comforce offer and vote in favor of the merger.
The acquisition, which has been approved by directors of both companies, is subject to certain conditions, including completion of financing and regulatory approvals.
Closing is expected in the fourth quarter. The acquisition will be accounted for under the purchase method.

Comforce said it intends to promptly file with the Securities and Exchange Commission to register the common stock to be issued in the deal. The tender offer will start when the registration statement is declared effective by the SEC.

Comforce said it has engaged National Westminster Bank Plc's Gleacher NatWest Inc to act as its financial adviser in connection with arranging acquisition financing of up to $125 million. The financing is expected to be completed within 60 days, it said.

In addition, the company said it is working with its senior lender, Fleet Financial Group Inc, to modify and expand its senior credit facility to support the consolidated operations of the businesses.

Comforce said John Fanning, Uniforce chairman and chief executive officer, and Rosemary Maniscalco, Uniforce president and chief operating officer, will continue to operate Uniforce's businesses following the merger. Comforce's senior management team will remain unchanged, with James Paterek serving as chairman, Christopher Franco serving as chief executive officer and Michael Ferrentino serving as president.
